backlog.spec: Clean each SMILES before featurization so that counterions and solvates do not distort the descriptors. In featurize, after Chem.MolFromSmiles, keep only the largest fragment by heavy-atom count (Chem.GetMolFrags(m, asMols=True) and pick the max, falling back to the whole molecule if fragmentation fails), then neutralize nothing else and recompute all descriptors on that fragment. If the molecule fails to parse, fall back to a zero row as now. Everything else (LightGBM settings, quantile transform, SVR, 50/50 blend) stays identical. This is a pure input-cleaning change and should cost no extra runtime.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest-fragment canonicalization

backlog.spec: Add a KNeighborsRegressor (k=7, weights='distance', metric euclidean) fitted on the quantile-normalized descriptors Str already computed for the SVR. Blend as 0.4 LightGBM + 0.4 SVR + 0.2 kNN.
backlog.title: kNN third blend member

backlog.spec: Change only the LightGBM hyperparameters: n_estimators=1500, learning_rate=0.01, num_leaves=15, max_depth=6, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, feature_fraction_bynode=0.5, min_child_samples=8, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1. The SVR member and the 50/50 blend stay the same.
backlog.title: Slower, longer LightGBM with feature sampling per node

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training set once, with a seed-based shuffle, into 85% fit and 15% validation. Fit the LGBMRegressor on the 85% part with n_estimators=2000, learning_rate=0.03 and eval_set on the 15% part with eval_metric='l1'. Use callbacks=[lightgbm.early_stopping(100, verbose=False)] to find best_iteration. Then refit the LightGBM model on all training data with n_estimators set to round(1.1 * best_iteration). Keep the SVR member and the 50/50 blend unchanged. This replaces the fixed 500-tree count with a data-driven one.
backlog.title: Inner-holdout early stopping to choose LightGBM tree count

backlog.spec: Keep the SVR on the quantile-normalized RDKit descriptors only. Build extra features for LightGBM only: 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, as 0/1 array) and a 512-bit feature-invariant Morgan count fingerprint (radius 2, rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Concatenate them to the descriptor matrix for the LightGBM fit and predict, and leave the SVR input unchanged. Keep the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: MACCS+FCFP counts for LightGBM only

backlog.spec: Fit LightGBM first. Get out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set with 5-fold KFold (seeded). Fit the RBF SVR (C=3, eps=0.1) on the quantile-normalized descriptors to predict the OOF residual y minus oof. The final prediction is the LightGBM full-fit prediction plus 0.7 times the SVR residual prediction on the test set.
backlog.title: SVR on LightGBM residuals

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, build the LGBMRegressor with monotone_constraints set per feature. Look up the column index of each of these RDKit descriptor names in Descriptors.descList: TPSA (-1), NumHDonors (-1), NumHAcceptors (-1), MolWt (-1), MolLogP (+1). Leave all other features unconstrained (0). Build the vector with the same length as the featurized matrix, using the names from Descriptors.descList in order, and pass it as monotone_constraints with monotone_constraints_method='advanced'. Keep every other hyperparameter, the SVR blend and the 50/50 weights unchanged. The goal is to restrict the trees to physically plausible directions so they generalize across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on LightGBM for polarity and size descriptors

backlog.spec: Instead of averaging the two members, let the SVR model what LightGBM gets wrong. Build 5-fold out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set (KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=seed), same LightGBM settings), form residuals r = y - oof_pred, fit the RBF SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on the quantile-normal-scaled descriptors with target r, refit LightGBM on all training data, and predict p_lgb + svr.predict(Ste) for the test molecules. Shrink the correction by a factor 0.7 to guard against overfitting the residuals. Runtime is about 6 LightGBM fits per fold, which fits the budget.
backlog.title: Residual stacking: SVR on LightGBM out-of-fold residuals

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first fit a Ridge regression (alpha=10) on the quantile-normalized, kept descriptor matrix (use the same QuantileTransformer as the SVR branch) to predict y, using only the training data. Compute residuals r = y - ridge_prediction on the training set, and train the LightGBM member (unchanged hyperparameters) on r instead of y. The final LightGBM prediction is ridge_test_prediction + lgb_residual_prediction. Keep the SVR member on y and the 50/50 blend unchanged. The linear baseline captures the global trend in polarity and size, and the trees model the remaining nonlinear structure.
backlog.title: Physchem linear baseline with LightGBM on its residuals

backlog.spec: Change the LightGBM blend member to DART: boosting_type='dart', drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50, n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.05, and keep num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1. The SVR member and the 50/50 blend stay the same.
backlog.title: LightGBM with DART boosting

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan generator with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=1024, includeChirality=True) and compute count fingerprints with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Add ring-membership information by building a second generator with atomInvariantsGenerator from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen() only for radius 1, appended as 256 bits. Concatenate these count features to the existing RDKit descriptors for the LightGBM member only. The SVR member keeps the descriptors only, as now. Keep all hyperparameters and the 50/50 blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Morgan fingerprints with chirality and ring-membership invariants for the tree member

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with an average of 8 SVRs (C=3, eps=0.1). Each is trained on a random 60% subset of the quantile-normalized descriptor columns, drawn with np.random.RandomState(seed+i). Average their predictions and use that as the SVR side of the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: SVR feature-subset bagging

backlog.spec: Change the final blend to 0.4 times the LightGBM prediction plus 0.6 times the SVR prediction. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Blend weight 0.4/0.6 toward SVR

backlog.spec: Add a KNeighborsRegressor (n_neighbors=7, weights='distance', Euclidean metric) fitted on the same quantile-normalized, constant-column-filtered descriptor matrix Str that the SVR uses. Predict on Ste. Change the final blend to 0.45 * LightGBM + 0.45 * SVR + 0.10 * kNN. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: kNN regressor as a third blend member

backlog.spec: Replace the single RBF SVR with an average of 5 SVRs, each trained on a random 60% subset of the kept (non-constant) descriptor columns, drawn with np.random.default_rng(seed). Fit the QuantileTransformer once on all kept columns as now, then index the scaled matrices by each column subset; each SVR keeps kernel='rbf', C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale'. Average the 5 test predictions into a single svr prediction and keep the 50/50 blend with LightGBM. This decorrelates the kernel member at roughly 5x the SVR cost, which is small relative to the 10-minute budget.
backlog.title: Feature-subset bagging for the SVR

backlog.spec: The two members are currently averaged 50/50 with no evidence that this is the optimum, and the pure-SVR run (0.3849) was much worse than pure LightGBM-ish baselines, so the optimum may sit slightly off centre. Change the final line to 0.4 * p_lgb + 0.6 * svr.predict(Ste). Change nothing else. This is a one-number edit; it settles the direction of the weight so later ideas need not guess.
backlog.title: Shift the blend weight toward the SVR

backlog.spec: After fitting the LightGBM member (unchanged hyperparameters), call model.predict(X, pred_leaf=True) on the training and test descriptor matrices to get leaf indices per tree. One-hot encode the leaf indices with sklearn OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') fitted on the training part. Fit an SVR (kernel='rbf', C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on these sparse leaf-indicator features, with the training targets y. Use the SVR prediction as the second blend member in place of the current descriptor SVR, keeping the 50/50 weights. The leaves act as learned, target-aware descriptor bins that the kernel can smooth over.
backlog.title: LightGBM leaf embeddings as input to an RBF SVR

backlog.spec: Add a third member: LGBMRegressor(linear_tree=True, linear_lambda=1.0, n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=4, min_child_samples=30, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.8, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1) trained on a compact slice of the descriptor matrix: the columns of Descriptors.descList named MolLogP, MolMR, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, RingCount, NumAromaticRings, LabuteASA, BalabanJ, BertzCT, qed, MaxPartialCharge, MinPartialCharge. Select the columns by name from descList. Final blend: 0.4 * LightGBM + 0.4 * SVR + 0.2 * linear-tree model.
backlog.title: Linear-tree LightGBM as a third blend member on a compact physchem set

memo: Helped: richer features and boosting. Descriptors plus Morgan counts cut loss from 0.4417 to 0.3917, and LightGBM gave 0.3722. The only accepted blend was LightGBM 50/50 with an RBF SVR on quantile-normalized descriptors (0.3650/0.3656, incumbent 0.3653). Did not help: model swaps (CatBoost 0.3894, 0.3682 as blend member; RF 0.3903; XGBoost 0.3808), pure SVR (0.3849), Tanimoto kernels (0.3764, 0.4176), GP (0.3690), MLP (0.3687), 3D shape (0.3675), SMARTS (0.3654), SVR retuning (0.3826, 0.3664). Within noise (sd ~0.0037): seed bagging (0.3646, 0.3653), learned blend weights (0.3635). Closest candidate: MACCS plus feature-Morgan counts (0.3599/0.3615 over 2 runs), rejected despite ~0.004 gain. Next: retry that feature addition in the blend, possibly with only LightGBM seeing it while the SVR keeps descriptors only. Replicate any gain under ~0.004. Avoid repeating seed bagging, blend weights, kernel swaps, SVR tuning, Huber.
